# Malaise

Malaise is a programming language that combines the worst design decisions
from fifty years of real languages, on purpose.

This organisation contains its projects: the interpreter, the specification,
the seven mutually incompatible package managers, the build system (which has
an eighth package manager), the documentation generator (which deletes the
documentation), and the formatter (which changes what your program does).

New here? Read [`interpreter/`](../../interpreter/) for the language
reference, then [`spec/`](../../spec/) for the parts that are wrong.

Contributions are welcome. The RFC process has a median time-to-decision of
41 months and a modal outcome of "postponed".
